hook: 95,851 people already solved your onion problem for $25.

scenes.visual_prompt: Overhead shot of a cluttered cutting board: half-chopped onions, scattered carrot peels, one visibly dull knife catching dim light.
scenes.voiceover: Thanksgiving's 12 days out and my cutting board already looks like this.

scenes.visual_prompt: Clean graphic card styled like an Amazon listing snippet: '95,851 ratings · 4.5 stars · $24.97' over a product shot of the Fullstar Pro chopper.
scenes.voiceover: This chopper has almost 100,000 ratings — that's not a launch spike, that's survived.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up hand loading a whole onion into the chopper hopper, pressing down once, diced onion dropping cleanly into the attached catch container.
scenes.voiceover: Load it, press once, get a uniform dice in about the time it takes to hand-chop a quarter of an onion.

scenes.visual_prompt: Four small bowls lined up: evenly diced onion, carrot, celery, and bell pepper — the mirepoix base — shot from directly above.
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers say onions, carrots, celery, and peppers come out evenly sized every single time.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split shot: a tomato turning mushy instead of diced in the chopper, then a close-up of the blade grid with food residue stuck in the gaps.
scenes.on_screen_text: The catch: soft produce gets mushy.
scenes.voiceover: It's built for firm vegetables — tomatoes and avocado aren't its job, and the blades need a careful hand-wash.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text-forward closing card with the five compared products thumbnailed in a row and an arrow pointing to 'link in bio'.
scenes.on_screen_text: Full breakdown + 4 more tools → link in bio.
scenes.voiceover: I lined this up against four other under-$25 Thanksgiving prep tools — full breakdown's on the blog.

caption: Thanksgiving is 12 days out and my cutting board is already a crime scene. I pulled the actual Amazon numbers on the $24.97 chopper with 95,851 ratings before deciding if it earns counter space — plus 4 more under-$25 prep tools I compared against it. Full breakdown on the blog (link in bio).
